principle.directDescription: Each vernier division is one least count shorter than a main division.
principle.retrogradeDescription: Each vernier division is one least count longer, so the numbering runs backwards.
principle.extendedDescription: Each vernier division is one least count short of two main divisions, spreading the marks out.

caliper.zeroErrorHint: A caliper that does not read zero when closed reports every length wrong by the same amount.

instruments.micrometerNote: The sleeve vernier resolves the 0.01 mm thimble into ten parts.
instruments.protractorNote: Twelve vernier divisions span 23 degrees, so the least count is five arcminutes.

practice.incorrect: Not quite — look again at which line coincides.
practice.unparseable: That is not a reading this instrument can give.
practice.zeroErrorPrompt: Correct for the zero error, then type the true measurement.

screenSummary.playArea: A main scale runs across the play area with a vernier scale sliding beneath it. A magnified view below shows the region around the line where the two scales coincide.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area sets how many divisions the vernier has and which of the three vernier geometries it uses, and has a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move the vernier along the main scale and watch which vernier line comes into alignment.

principle.currentDetails: The vernier has {{divisions}} divisions, so one least count is {{leastCount}}. The vernier zero sits past {{main}}, vernier line {{index}} coincides, and the reading is {{reading}}.

controls.vernierHelp: Right and left arrows move the vernier one least count. Page Up and Page Down move it one main division.

screenSummary.playArea: A vernier caliper holds a workpiece between its jaws. Below it, the caliper's scales are shown full width, with a magnified view of the region around the coinciding line.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area chooses the caliper's scale and which jaws are measuring, sets a zero error, and has a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move the jaws and read the measurement off the two scales.

caliper.currentDetails: Measuring with the {{mode}} on the {{scale}} scale. The main scale reads past {{main}}, vernier line {{index}} coincides, and the measurement is {{reading}}.

controls.jawsHelp: Right and left arrows open and close the jaws by one least count. Page Up and Page Down move them one main division.

screenSummary.playArea: An instrument other than a caliper is shown with its vernier scale: either a micrometer, whose vernier reads a rotating thimble, or a bevel protractor, whose scale is a circle.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area chooses the instrument and has a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move the instrument's scale and read it the same way you read a caliper.

instruments.currentDetails: The {{instrument}} reads past {{main}}, vernier line {{index}} coincides, and the reading is {{reading}}.

controls.scaleHelp: Right and left arrows move the scale one least count. Page Up and Page Down move it one main division.

screenSummary.playArea: An instrument is set to a value for you to read, shown full width with a magnified view of the coinciding line beneath it.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a field for your answer, a Check button, a New question button, a question type selector, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Read the instrument, type what it says, and check your answer.

controls.answerHelp: Type the reading, then activate the Check button.

responses.incorrect: Not correct. Look again at which vernier line coincides.
responses.unparseable: That is not a reading this instrument can give.

preferences.startMagnified: Start with the magnified view shown

keyboardHelp.title: Move the Vernier
keyboardHelp.ends: Jump to zero or to full scale
